title: Lens remediation ingestion
objective: Make remediation and recertification provenance verifiable and actionable in Kyro Lens while closing the replay-integrity gap that Lens will consume.

phases.title: Replay integrity
phases.objective: Close the unsafe snapshot handoff before a reader consumes the protocol.

tasks.title: Validate every replay snapshot before reuse
tasks.description: Harden multi-record remediation replay so a non-final record.result.snapshot is never used as the next replay base unless its canonical business-state digest equals record.result.stateSha256.
tasks.context: Resolves debt-2. Preserve ADR-0003: the first remediation may originate from a genuinely drifted live base, but a forged intermediate snapshot must still make doctor/status diverged. Keep debt-3 open: this task validates the current snapshot representation and must not redesign immutable record storage without a dedicated protocol decision.
acceptance_criteria: Every non-final snapshot is structurally valid and its canonical business-state digest is verified before it becomes the replay base.
A valid multi-record chain from a genuinely drifted first base remains remediated or recertified as appropriate.
Tampering an intermediate snapshot or its declared digest yields diverged in doctor and status, with no historical artifact mutation.
Focused remediation and verification harnesses cover the regression and pass.

evidence.summary: Validated every non-final remediation snapshot as a strict SprintFile and verified its canonical business-state digest before replay reuse.
validation: Independent certification: npm run check complete (pass)
evidence.notes: Independent certification verified the new regression fails without the replay guard. The protocol comment now points to that guardrail; the original contract intentionally preserves the snapshot as archival data.

phases.title: Lens protocol reader
phases.objective: Give Lens a strict, read-only interpretation of the versioned remediation and certification protocol.

tasks.title: Model and parse remediation protocol shapes in Lens
tasks.description: Add strongly typed Lens representations and fail-closed parsing for remediation anchors, R-NNN records, certification anchors, and C-NNN records without weakening legacy sprint compatibility.
tasks.context: Lens is a read-only consumer. Support protocol version 1 only; unknown versions, unknown keys in closed records, malformed digests, invalid anchor identity/path shapes, and bare declared verdicts are parse failures, never permissive unknown payloads. Existing scopes without remediation fields must remain readable.
acceptance_criteria: Lens has explicit discriminated types for v1 remediation and recertification structures rather than unknown or any payloads.
A legacy sprint without remediation data still parses exactly as before.
A well-formed v1 remediated or recertified sprint parses, while malformed, unknown-version, and unknown-key protocol records are rejected with field-specific diagnostics.
Lens parser tests cover valid and rejected protocol shapes.

tasks.title: Resolve and verify anchored provenance in Lens
tasks.description: Implement the read-only resolver that follows each remediation anchor through remediations[].path and validates its identity, scope containment, commitment, ordering, certificate chain-head binding, and evidence references before producing a Lens provenance summary.
tasks.context: The remediation anchor path is authoritative only when it is scope-contained and names the same R-NNN id as the anchor; Lens must not discover alternate files or silently select a different record. Reuse Kyro AI's canonical commitment rules through shared contract fixtures, not a looser reader-only interpretation. Records and evidence are read only and are never applied, repaired, or rewritten by Lens.
acceptance_criteria: A valid ordered chain resolves to a provenance summary containing the historical issue, remediation rationale, typed operations, current verification state, and optional certification.

Path traversal, anchor/id disagreement, content or commitment mismatch, broken chain order, stale certificate head, unreadable evidence, and unsupported version return an actionable integrity or unsupported result.
The Lens corpus includes validated remediation and certification artifacts when present and records a read failure instead of inventing content when they are not valid.
The resolver performs no workspace writes.

evidence.summary: Implemented Lens read-only v1 provenance verification with canonical SHA-256 commitments, ordered remediation chains, certification/evidence validation, and bounded derived corpus summaries.

evidence.notes: Per approved E3/E4 correction, Lens never injects raw remediation/certification records, snapshots, or evidence bodies into the AI corpus; it emits only a bounded derived summary and failures for invalid provenance.

phases.title: Lens provenance presentation
phases.objective: Expose trustworthy remediation status without representing historical evidence as corrected state.

tasks.title: Render remediation and recertification provenance
tasks.description: Add a read-only overview surface for valid remediation/recertification provenance and a distinct actionable failure state for diverged or unsupported chains.
tasks.context: Follow the existing checkpoint-summary pattern: Lens observes immutable history and never offers repair. A failing remediation chain must not disappear behind an apparently healthy checkpoint card or stale state. Keep diagnostic text concrete enough to identify the bad record/path without rendering untrusted payload as trusted provenance.
acceptance_criteria: A valid remediated chain visibly names its R-NNN provenance, original issue, rationale, operations, and remediated state.
A valid recertified chain additionally names its C-NNN and the evidence/verdict provenance bound to the current head.
Diverged and unsupported inputs render a distinct diagnostic surface and never fall back to presenting the original close as valid current state.
Component tests cover loading, valid remediated, valid recertified, diverged, and unsupported states.

phases.title: Cross-repository certification
phases.objective: Prove writer, installed runtime, and reader agree on the protocol without claiming publication readiness.

tasks.title: Exercise the Kyro AI to Lens contract end to end
tasks.description: Create shared, deterministic contract fixtures from real Kyro remediation and recertification output and prove Lens loads valid data while rejecting representative invalid chains.
tasks.context: The fixture must travel through real Kyro CLI close/remediate/recertify behavior rather than a hand-written happy-path record. Cover remediated-without-certificate, recertified, unsupported schema, changed record bytes/commitment, anchor/path mismatch, and stale certification after a new remediation. No test may require Lens to mutate artifacts.
acceptance_criteria: A real valid Kyro fixture is rendered by Lens as remediated and, after certification, recertified with matching provenance.
Every invalid fixture fails closed in Lens with a specific diagnostic and no stale-state fallback.
Kyro AI and Lens focused suites pass from their respective checkouts.

emergentTasks.title: Verify Lens v1 provenance against canonical vectors
emergentTasks.description: Correct T3.3 by implementing a strict, read-only v1 verifier instead of trusting an anchor-shaped record. It must use canonical JSON and SHA-256, exact closed-record validation, record and anchor containment rules, evidence semantics, and real Kyro conformance vectors before Lens may claim verified remediation or recertification provenance.
emergentTasks.context: Implements ADR-0004 and S14. This replaces the loose reader-only interpretation implied by T3.3 with an explicitly conformant v1 verifier.
acceptance_criteria: Lens accepts only v1 closed record shapes and lower-case 64-hex digests; unknown keys or versions, unavailable cryptography, bad commitment, broken record ordering, and stale certificate head are unsupported or diverged, never valid.

Remediation and certification records and their anchors are scope-contained archive references with matching identities; external artifact evidence is workspace-contained, while kyro-task-verdict evidence is re-derived from the current sprint state.

Canonical SHA-256 and state/chain evaluation match checked-in real Kyro conformance vectors including a genuine divergence and an active later sprint; Lens never labels a chain remediated or recertified based only on anchor shape.
The verifier and all readers remain read-only.
